title: Omaha–Ponca language - Wikipedia
text: Omaha–Ponca is a Siouan language spoken by the Omaha people of Nebraska and the Ponca people of Oklahoma and Nebraska. The two dialects differ minimally but are considered distinct languages by their speakers.

title: Omaha-Ponca Language - Sam Noble Museum
text: Ponca and the mutually intelligible variety Omaha were first encountered along the Missouri River in Nebraska. Omaha-Ponca is a member of the Dhegiha branch of the Siouan-Catawban language family. Closely related Dhegiha languages include Kansa, Quapaw, and Osage.

title: Omaha–Ponca language - Сommunity Hub
text: Omaha–Ponca is a daughter language to the Siouan mother language but has developed some of its own rules for nasalization and aspiration. What were once allophones in Proto-Siouan have become phonemes in the Omaha–Ponca language.
